body_text: Theorem 1.1 (Heine-Borel). A subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is compact if and only if it is closed and bounded.
body_tokens: Theorem Heine-Borel A subset of mathbb_R n is compact if and only if it is closed and bounded

body_text: Remark 1.2. The forward direction fails in infinite-dimensional normed spaces, where closed bounded sets need not be compact.
body_tokens: Remark The forward direction fails in infinite-dimensional normed spaces where closed bounded sets need not be compact

body_text: Proof. Reduce to the case of a closed box via boundedness, then apply the finite-subcover argument to a bisection sequence. The converse follows from continuity of the coordinate projections.
